caption:
Sign before touring? Read this first.

In Ontario, a buyer representation agreement should be in writing and presented to you as soon as possible, and it should explain your services, what you will pay, how long it lasts and whether you can cancel it. 1) Find the expiry date, which must appear prominently on the first page. 2) Make sure every service you expect is written in. 3) Ask how your Realtor® is paid and what changes if a seller covers some of it. 4) Ask how the agreement can end and what a holdover clause means for you. If anything is unclear, ask before you sign.
Source: RECO, "Signing a contract with a real estate brokerage" (reco.on.ca) and RECO Bulletin 2.3, checked Nov 21, 2026.

Sold in Oakville? Report it, even if no tax is owing.

The Canada Revenue Agency says the sale of a principal residence must be reported on your tax return, even when the principal residence exemption means no tax is owing. 1) Keep your purchase and sale documents and records of major improvements. 2) Report the sale on your tax return for the year you sold. 3) Designate the home as your principal residence on Schedule 3, plus Form T2091 where the CRA asks for it. 4) If you forgot or are not sure, ask an accountant: the CRA may deny the exemption if the sale is not reported, and a late-designation penalty may apply.
Source: Canada Revenue Agency, "Reporting the sale of your principal residence for individuals" (canada.ca), checked Nov 21, 2026.

Brampton: $500K mortgage. What does an extra $200 a month do?

Example only, computed with Canadian semi-annual compounding:
1) $500,000 mortgage at 4.44%, 25-year amortization: about $2,751 a month.
2) Add $200 a month: $2,951 a month.
3) The mortgage is paid off in 266 months (22 years 2 months) instead of 300, almost 3 years sooner.
4) Total interest falls from about $325,214 to about $282,820, roughly $42,394 less (about $42,400).
4.44% is nesto.ca's lowest 5-year fixed insured rate as of Nov 21, 2026. Your rate depends on your lender and down payment, and rates change at renewal. Many lenders limit prepayments, so check your prepayment privileges first.

caption:
Etobicoke: offered asking. Still lost?

The asking price is where a home starts, not always where it ends. Homes can sell above or below it. 1) Ask your Realtor® for recent sold prices of similar homes nearby, not just list prices. 2) Decide your top price with your lender before offer night. 3) Remember an offer is more than price: the deposit, closing date and conditions count too. 4) Get advice before waiving any protection.
